head: Netflix no longer available on older Sony Blu-ray players and receivers
dek: Sony switched off network services such as Netflix and Spotify on a list of older Blu-ray players, AV receivers, soundbars, home theatre systems and speakers on 17 November. Downloaded services and their icons may stop working or disappear from 18 November.
details: Which services end depends on the model; the list includes Netflix, Spotify, Pandora, Slacker Radio and Vudu. Models named include the STR-DN1050, STR-DN1060, STR-DN1070 and STR-DN1080 receivers, the HT-CT790, HT-CT800 and HT-ST5000 soundbars, the BDP-S370, BDP-S570 and BDP-S780 Blu-ray players and the SRS-X7 speaker. Sony first posted the notice in mid-May and updated it on 6 August; it's Sony support article 00398725. Not every listed model was sold in every country, and it's not every Sony product.
where: Listed older Sony audio and video products, from 17 November 2026
means: If you watch Netflix or play Spotify through an older Sony player, receiver or soundbar, those apps may be gone from it now, and you'll need another device for them.
todo: Look up your model in Sony support article 00398725. If it's listed, use a streaming stick, a smart TV's own apps or your phone for those services.
